## Where we are

::: {.incremental}
- Prediction (A8) asked **who** is at risk. Today: **what would happen if we intervened?**
- By the end you can:
  - state a **causal question** and the **estimand**
  - draw a **DAG** and name **confounders, mediators, colliders**
  - let the DAG choose the **adjustment set**
:::

## Our question: did the programme lower blood pressure?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- **3,000 adults with hypertension** from routine clinic records (synthetic)
- **1,229 (41%) enrolled** in a community health-worker **programme**: **not randomised**
- Outcome: **SBP at 12 months**
- Also recorded: age, sex, education, urban, BMI, diabetes, **baseline SBP**, **adherence** at 6 months, **clinic visits** in the year
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
htn |> select(age, diabetes, baseline_sbp, programme, adherent, clinic_visits, sbp_12m) |> head(6)
```
:::
:::

# Topic 1 — The naive comparison {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Enrolled vs not enrolled

```{r}
htn |> group_by(programme) |> summarise(n = n(), sbp_12m = round(mean(sbp_12m), 1), age = round(mean(age), 1), baseline_sbp = round(mean(baseline_sbp), 1), diabetes = round(mean(diabetes), 2))
```

::: {.warn}
SBP at 12 months is **142 vs 143**: a difference of **−1.4 mmHg**. "The programme hardly works"? But the enrolled were **older**, had a **higher baseline SBP (157 vs 150)** and **more diabetes (25% vs 13%)**. Sicker people enrol: **confounding by indication**. The groups were **never comparable**.
:::

## Potential outcomes

::: {.eq}
Y¹ = SBP if enrolled      Y⁰ = SBP if not enrolled      effect for one person = Y¹ − Y⁰
:::

::: {.incremental}
- We only ever see **one** of the two for each person: the **fundamental problem** of causal inference
- **ATE** = average of Y¹ − Y⁰ over **everybody** (what if all enrolled vs none?)
- **ATT** = average over **those who enrolled** (did it help them?)
- A **randomised trial** makes the groups exchangeable. In observational data we need **assumptions**: **no unmeasured confounding** (exchangeability given covariates), **positivity** (everyone could get either option), **consistency** (a well-defined intervention)
:::

# Topic 2 — DAGs {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Three roles a variable can play

| Role | Structure | Adjust? |
|---|---|---|
| **Confounder** | C → exposure and C → outcome | **Yes**: closes a back-door path |
| **Mediator** | exposure → M → outcome | **No** for the total effect (it removes part of the effect) |
| **Collider** | exposure → K ← outcome | **No**: adjusting **opens** a biasing path |

::: {.key}
Here: **baseline SBP, age, diabetes, education** are confounders; **adherence** is a **mediator** (the programme works partly by improving adherence); **clinic visits** are a **collider** (the programme brings people in, and so does poor BP).
:::

## The DAG in R

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4
g <- dagitty("dag {
  programme -> sbp_12m ; programme -> adherent -> sbp_12m
  programme -> clinic_visits ; sbp_12m -> clinic_visits
  age -> programme ; age -> sbp_12m ; diabetes -> programme ; diabetes -> sbp_12m
  baseline_sbp -> programme ; baseline_sbp -> sbp_12m
  education -> programme ; education -> sbp_12m ; education -> adherent
  urban -> programme ; urban -> bmi ; bmi -> sbp_12m ; bmi -> baseline_sbp ; bmi -> diabetes
  age -> baseline_sbp ; age -> diabetes
}")
plot(graphLayout(g))
```

## Let the DAG choose

```{r}
adjustmentSets(g, exposure = "programme", outcome = "sbp_12m", effect = "total")
descendants(g, "programme")
```

::: {.incremental}
- Two **minimal sufficient sets**: {age, baseline SBP, BMI, diabetes, education} or {age, baseline SBP, diabetes, education, urban}
- **Never** adjust for **descendants** of the exposure (adherent, clinic_visits) when you want the **total** effect
- The DAG encodes **assumptions**, mostly the **arrows you left out**; the data cannot prove it. Draw it **before** the analysis, from subject knowledge
:::

## What a DAG does not do

::: {.warn}
- It cannot show **unmeasured** confounders you did not think of (here an unrecorded "motivation" exists)
- It says **what** to adjust for, not **how** (functional form, interactions: A6)
- Selecting covariates by **p-values** or stepwise methods is **not** a causal strategy
:::

## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("z1q1", "Enrolled adults had a higher baseline SBP and more diabetes. Why can the naive difference in 12-month SBP not be read as the effect?",
         c("The sample of 3,000 adults is too small to estimate a difference between two means",
           "The groups differed before the programme, so outcomes would differ anyway",
           "The outcome was measured at 12 months and not at the time of enrolment in the programme",
           "The naive difference has a confidence interval, and causal effects do not have one"), answer = 2,
         explain = "Baseline differences that also affect the outcome are confounding: the comparison mixes the effect of the programme with the effect of being sicker.")
```

## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("z1q2", "What is the average treatment effect (ATE)?",
         c("The mean difference between the enrolled and the non-enrolled adults as observed",
           "The mean benefit among the adults who actually enrolled in the programme",
           "The mean difference if everybody were enrolled versus nobody enrolled",
           "The largest effect that is seen in any of the subgroups of the cohort"), answer = 3,
         explain = "The ATE averages the individual effects Y1 - Y0 over the whole population. The effect in those who enrolled is the ATT.")
```

## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("z1q3", "Adherence is improved by the programme and lowers SBP. If you want the total effect of the programme, should you adjust for adherence?",
         c("Yes: it is a confounder, since it is related to both variables",
           "Yes: adjusting for more variables makes the estimate less biased",
           "No: adherence was measured after baseline, so it carries no information",
           "No: it is a mediator, and adjusting removes part of the effect"), answer = 4,
         explain = "A mediator lies on the causal path. Conditioning on it blocks that path and leaves the direct effect only.")
```

## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("z1q4", "Clinic visits are increased by the programme and by a high SBP. What happens if you adjust for clinic visits?",
         c("A biasing path is opened, because clinic visits are a collider",
           "The confounding by baseline SBP is removed more completely than before",
           "Nothing changes, because clinic visits are not a cause of the 12-month SBP",
           "The estimate becomes the direct effect of the programme on blood pressure"), answer = 1,
         explain = "Conditioning on a common effect of exposure and outcome creates an association between them that is not causal: collider bias.")
```

## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("z1q5", "What is the best source for the arrows in a DAG?",
         c("The p-values of the associations between the variables found in the data",
           "Subject knowledge about how the variables arise, set down in advance",
           "A stepwise selection procedure applied to all of the measured variables",
           "The correlation matrix of the variables, with a cut-off of 0.3 for an arrow"), answer = 2,
         explain = "A DAG states causal assumptions. Data show associations, which cannot distinguish a confounder from a mediator or a collider.")
```

## Score and take-home

**Your score: <span class="quiz-score"></span>**

::: {.incremental}
- **Causal question** → estimand (**ATE**, **ATT**) → assumptions
- **Confounder**: adjust. **Mediator, collider**: do not (for the total effect)
- **DAG first**, from subject knowledge; `adjustmentSets()`
- The naive comparison is **confounded by indication**
- A DAG cannot reveal **unmeasured** confounders
:::
